evals.prompt: How do I integrate freeRASP in my Flutter app to detect if it's running on a rooted Android device?

assertions.description: Response references TalsecConfig with AndroidConfig.expectedPackageName and expectedSigningCertificateHashes
assertions.expected: TalsecConfig + AndroidConfig setup with expectedPackageName and expectedSigningCertificateHashes

assertions.description: Response references onRootDetected callback and routing to RaspBloc or equivalent handler
assertions.expected: onRootDetected callback that dispatches a threat event (e.g., RaspEvent.threatDetected(RaspThreat.root))

assertions.description: Response includes Talsec.instance.start() call placed before runApp in main.dart

evals.prompt: What should my app do when freeRASP detects a Frida hooking attack? Should I just log it?

assertions.description: Response explicitly says logging alone is NOT sufficient for hook detection
assertions.expected: No — logging alone is insufficient. Hook/Frida detection is a critical threat requiring the app to block operations or terminate.

assertions.description: Response recommends blocking the app and references the threat response table or equivalent guidance
assertions.expected: Block the app immediately for onHookDetected — active attack in progress

assertions.description: Response warns against calling exit() directly from the callback and recommends dispatching to BLoC
assertions.expected: Dispatch via _bloc.add(RaspEvent.threatDetected(RaspThreat.hook)) — do not call exit() directly in the callback

evals.prompt: How do I configure freeRASP so it works in debug mode without blocking the development emulator?

assertions.description: Response explains isProd: kReleaseMode (false in debug) to disable strict checks
assertions.expected: isProd: kReleaseMode is set to false automatically in debug mode, disabling strict checks

assertions.description: Response explains that the emulator threat should be handled conditionally — blocked in production, allowed in debug
assertions.expected: onEmulatorDetected can be ignored or not block when kReleaseMode is false

assertions.description: Response mentions including the debug signing certificate hash in expectedSigningCertificateHashes
assertions.expected: Incluir el hash del certificado de debug en expectedSigningCertificateHashes con guarda if (!kReleaseMode)

evals.prompt: I need to be able to swap freeRASP for a commercial RASP solution later without touching my BLoC or domain code. How?

assertions.description: Response describes the RaspProvider abstract interface in the domain layer
assertions.expected: Define an abstract interface class RaspProvider in the domain layer that BLoC depends on

assertions.description: Response explains FreeRaspAdapter implementing RaspProvider in the data layer
assertions.expected: FreeRaspAdapter implements RaspProvider in the data layer — BLoC never imports freeRASP SDK directly

assertions.description: Response explains that swapping providers only requires changing the DI binding
assertions.expected: To swap, only the DI binding changes: bind RaspProvider → CommercialRaspAdapter — no BLoC or domain changes needed

evals.prompt: How do I extract the signing certificate hash needed for freeRASP's expectedSigningCertificateHashes config?

assertions.description: Response provides at least one concrete shell command to extract the base64-encoded SHA-256 hash
assertions.expected: Shell command using keytool, apksigner, or Play Console SHA-256 converted with xxd -r -p | base64

assertions.description: Response mentions the Play Console path for release builds (App Signing Key Certificate → SHA-256)
assertions.expected: Play Console → Setup → App Signing → App Signing Key Certificate → SHA-256

assertions.description: Response clarifies the need to include both release and debug hashes during development
assertions.expected: Include both the release hash and the debug hash (guarded with if (!kReleaseMode)) during development

evals.prompt: Does this skill cover certificate pinning?

assertions.description: Response clearly states that certificate pinning is out of scope for this skill
assertions.expected: No — certificate pinning is outside the scope of flutter-rasp-strategy

assertions.description: Response redirects the user to the flutter-certificate-pinning skill
assertions.expected: Refer to the flutter-certificate-pinning skill for TLS/certificate pinning implementation

assertions.description: Response briefly explains what this skill does cover (RASP / MASVS-RESILIENCE)
assertions.expected: This skill covers runtime threat detection (root, hook, tamper, emulator) under OWASP MASVS-RESILIENCE
